title: Development Versus Production
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of development versus production and identify at least two of its listed subtopics.
Trace the worked example for development versus production and describe its expected result.
Select a focused test or verification step for a normal case and a meaningful failure boundary.

content.intro: Explore development versus production through the source syllabus topics, a small inspectable example, and a practical verification task. The example is teaching material, not a claim that the platform executed Flask code.
content.why_it_matters: Development Versus Production helps operate an application safely outside the developer’s machine. Production readiness requires observable behavior, controlled failure, recovery evidence and safe configuration.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Development Versus Production helps operate an application safely outside the developer’s machine. Production readiness requires observable behavior, controlled failure, recovery evidence and safe configuration.

content_blocks.title: What to learn
content_blocks.text: This lesson covers: Different server requirements; Debugging and configuration changes; Production-safe error handling. Keep the source terms intact; for each one, name the component that owns the behavior, the inputs/assumptions, and the expected result.

items.title: Different server requirements
items.text: For different server requirements, identify the component responsible, the input it receives, and the observable result it should produce.

items.title: Debugging and configuration changes
items.text: Make the configuration source and load order explicit so tests and deployments do not accidentally inherit unsafe defaults.

items.title: Production-safe error handling
items.text: Return a safe external response while preserving diagnostic context in controlled server logs.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Development Versus Production
content_blocks.expected_output: A POST /preferences stores a small preference in Flask’s signed session cookie. Do not place passwords, private tokens, or sensitive records in the default client-side session.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Set FLASK_SECRET_KEY to a generated secret in the environment; use HTTPS and enable SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE in production.

content_blocks.title: Before using this beyond practice
content_blocks.text: Validate untrusted input at the server boundary, keep secrets out of source code, and test the failure path. Optional extensions or hosting infrastructure are separate dependencies unless stated otherwise.

content.expected_result: A POST /preferences stores a small preference in Flask’s signed session cookie. Do not place passwords, private tokens, or sensitive records in the default client-side session.
content.run_instructions: Set FLASK_SECRET_KEY to a generated secret in the environment; use HTTPS and enable SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE in production.
troubleshooting: Confirm the expected virtual environment and installed dependency versions before diagnosing framework behavior.
Check route/method, input shape, status code, traceback location and relevant configuration one at a time.
For database or third-party integration examples, use isolated local resources and explicit timeouts; do not use production credentials.
content.reset_steps: Stop the local development server, reset only disposable local practice data if needed, and remove temporary artifacts created by the exercise. Never delete production data or migration history to reset practice.
content.try_it_yourself: Audit a Flask app for safe configuration/secrets, cookie settings, errors, request limits, production WSGI server, HTTPS/proxy settings, dependency review, health checks and rollback documentation.
progressive_hints: Name the Flask component or ecosystem tool responsible for development versus production.
Run the smallest example in an isolated local project and compare the actual response with the stated expected result.
Add one negative or boundary test, then check the linked version-specific official documentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a fragment without checking its imports, app configuration or dependencies.
common_mistakes.why: Many Flask examples assume a configured app and a specific runtime or extension version.
common_mistakes.fix: Follow the run instructions, record the Flask/Python version and test the smallest behavior first.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the successful request path.
common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, unsupported methods, unauthorized objects and service failures often have different behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a negative or boundary test and assert the status code and response contract.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a local example as production-ready.
common_mistakes.why: Secret management, concurrency, deployment, monitoring and failure recovery need separate design decisions.
common_mistakes.fix: Review the matching deployment and security references before publication or real use.

content.recap: Development Versus Production connects Different server requirements; Debugging and configuration changes; Production-safe error handling. Verify the example under the selected environment and keep its assumptions visible.
content.accessibility_notes: Use descriptive headings, meaningful labels and alt text; provide a text explanation of the diagram; keep code selectable and keyboard navigable; never rely on color alone.
content.version_notes: Baseline: Flask 3.1.x, with the official changelog listing 3.1.3 on 2026-02-18. Verify current patch versions and ecosystem compatibility before use. Optional packages are not Flask built-ins.
content.task: Audit a Flask app for safe configuration/secrets, cookie settings, errors, request limits, production WSGI server, HTTPS/proxy settings, dependency review, health checks and rollback documentation.
task_acceptance_criteria: State the Python and Flask versions or the relevant non-Flask tool version.
Record expected and observed results for a normal case.
Test one invalid, unauthorized or boundary case and explain the status/result.
hints: Identify the main responsibility behind development versus production.
Keep request/data boundaries explicit and verify assumptions with a focused test.
Consult the linked official reference before using a version-sensitive API.
content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: trace one input through the relevant framework component, keep validation and authorization explicit, and write the smallest test that demonstrates the intended behavior. This note does not claim the example was executed.
summary: Development Versus Production is part of deployment and production operations and should be understood alongside its listed source subtopics.
The worked example is a focused fragment; use the stated context and dependencies before running it.
Verify expected and failure behavior locally and record the check so it can be reproduced.
